plan: 2 Kings 20:1-11; Isaiah 38:1-8; 2 Chronicles 32:24-31; Isaiah 38:9-22; 2 Kings 20:12-19; Isaiah 39:1-8

readings.title: The Verdict of Mortality
readings.subtitle: Facing the end of his biological life, Ḥizqiyahu appeals to his record of functional harmony and structural truth before YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:1] In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick unto death. And Yeshayahu the prophet, son of Amots, went to him and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Command <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> house, for you are going to die, and not live.’</dq> ” [2] And he turned his face toward the wall, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [3] “<dn>I</dn> pray to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, remember how <dn>I</dn> have walked before <dn>You</dn> in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done <dn>את</dn> what was good in <dn>Your</dn> eyes.” And Ḥizqiyahu wept bitterly.

readings.title: The Reversal of the Decree
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH responds to the weight of Ḥizqiyahu's petition, extending his timeline and guaranteeing the defense of the physical city.
readings.text: [4] And it came to be, before Yeshayahu had gone out into the middle court, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying, [5] “Return and say to Ḥizqiyahu the leader of <dn>My</dn> people, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Daviḏ your father, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> prayer, <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> tears. See, <dn>I</dn> am going to heal you. On the third day go up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. </dq>[6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall add to your days fifteen years, and deliver you and <dn>את</dn> this city from the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur, and shall defend <dn>את</dn> this city for <dn>My</dn> own sake, and for the sake of Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant.”</dq> ’ ”

readings.title: The Physical Agent of Healing
readings.subtitle: Yeshayahu deploys a localized biological remedy for the physical affliction, aligning natural elements with the divine decree of restoration.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:7] And Yeshayahu said, “Take a cake of figs.” And they took and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.

readings.title: The Geometrical Sign of Reversal
readings.subtitle: To authenticate the guarantee, YeHoVaH manipulates the celestial mechanics of the cosmos, moving the visible shadow backward.
readings.text: [8] And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “What is the sign that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does heal me, and that <dn>I</dn> shall go up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the third day?” [9] And Yeshayahu said, “This is the sign for you from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>He</dn> has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees or go backward ten degrees?” [10] And Ḥizqiyahu said, “It would be easy for the shadow to go down ten degrees; no, but let the shadow go backward ten degrees.” [11] And Yeshayahu the prophet cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down on the sundial of Aḥaz.

readings.title: The Agony of the Weaver's Loom
readings.subtitle: Ḥizqiyahu recounts his despair at the precipice of She’ol, recognizing the frailty of human biology under systemic affliction.
readings.text: [Isaiah 38:9] This is the writing of Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, when he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness: [10] <dn>I</dn> said, “Am <dn>I</dn> to go into the gates of She’ol in the prime of <dn>my</dn> life? Shall <dn>I</dn> be deprived of the rest of <dn>my</dn> years?” [11] <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>I</dn> shall not see <dn>Yah</dn> – <dn>Yah</dn> in the land of the living! <dn>I</dn> shall no longer look on man with <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the world! [12] “<dn>My</dn> dwelling is plucked up, taken from me like a shepherd’s tent. <dn>I</dn> have cut off <dn>my</dn> life like a weaver; <dn>He</dn> cuts me off from the loom. From day to night <dn>You</dn> make an end of me. [13] “<dn>I</dn> soothed myself until morning. Like a lion, so <dn>He</dn> shatters <dn>את</dn> all <dn>my</dn> bones. From day to night <dn>You</dn> make an end of me. [14] “Like a swallow or a thrush, so <dn>I</dn> chattered; <dn>I</dn> moaned like a dove; <dn>my</dn> eyes look weakly on high. O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am oppressed, undertake for me!

readings.title: The Praemium of the Living
readings.subtitle: Delivered from the pit of corruption, the sovereign acknowledges that restorative justice and thanksgiving belong exclusively to the living.
readings.text: [15] “What do <dn>I</dn> say? For <dn>He</dn> has spoken to me, and <dn>He</dn> Himself has acted. Softly <dn>I</dn> go, all <dn>my</dn> years, because of the bitterness of <dn>my</dn> being. [16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by these do men live, and <dn>my</dn> spirit finds life in all of them. Restore me and make me live. [17] “See, for peace <dn>I</dn> had what was bitter, bitter. But <dn>You</dn> have lovingly delivered <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> being from the pit of corruption, for <dn>You</dn> have cast <dn>את</dn> all <dn>my</dn> sins behind <dn>Your</dn> back. [18] “For She’ol does not thank <dn>You</dn>, nor death praise <dn>You</dn>; those who go down to the pit do not watch for <dn>Your</dn> truth. [19] “The living, the living – he is praising <dn>You</dn>, as <dn>I</dn> do this day. A father makes known <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> truth to his children. [20] “Come <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to save me! And let us sing <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”

readings.title: The Breach of Trust
readings.subtitle: Envoys from Baḇel, the engineered epicenter of systemic confusion, arrive, and Ḥizqiyahu foolishly exposes the totality of the kingdom's reserved wealth.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:12] At that time Beroḏaḵ-Balaḏan son of Balaḏan, sovereign of Baḇel, sent letters and a present to Ḥizqiyahu, for he heard that Ḥizqiyahu had been sick. [13] And Ḥizqiyahu listened to them, and showed them <dn>את</dn> all his treasure house, <dn>את</dn> the silver and <dn>את</dn> the gold, and <dn>את</dn> the spices and <dn>את</dn> the precious ointment, and <dn>את</dn> all his armoury, and <dn>את</dn> all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Ḥizqiyahu did not show them.

readings.title: The Test of the Lifted Heart
readings.subtitle: Despite massive physical increase and localized blessing, the sovereign's pride necessitates a withdrawal of divine oversight to reveal his true internal state.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 32:25] However, Ḥizqiyahu did not repay according to the good done to him, for his heart was lifted up, therefore wrath came upon him and upon Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim. [27] And Ḥizqiyahu had much riches and esteem. And he made himself treasuries for silver, and for gold, and for precious stones, and for spices, and for shields, and for all desirable utensils; [28] and storehouses for the harvest of grain, and wine, and oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and folds for flocks. [29] And he made cities for himself, and possessions of great numbers of flocks and herds, for <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him much property. [30] And Ḥizqiyahu himself had stopped <dn>את</dn> the upper outlet of the waters of Giḥon, and directed them to the west side of the City of Daviḏ. And Ḥizqiyahu prospered in all his work. [31] However with <dn>את</dn> the envoys of the princes of Baḇel, whom they sent to ask him about the wonder that was done in the land, <dn>Elohim</dn> left him, in order to try him, to know <dn>את</dn> all that was in his heart.

readings.title: The Decree of the Babylonian Captivity
readings.subtitle: Yeshayahu formally declares the legal consequence of the sovereign's vulnerability: the future extraction of Yehuḏah's wealth and lineage into the adversary's penal system.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:14] And Yeshayahu the prophet came to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu, and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?” And Ḥizqiyahu said, “They came from a distant land, from Baḇel.” [15] And he said, “What have they seen in your house?” And Ḥizqiyahu answered, “They saw all that is in my house; there is not an object among my treasures that <dn>I</dn> did not show them.” [16] And Yeshayahu said to Ḥizqiyahu, “Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: [17] <dq>See, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have treasured up until this day, shall be brought to Baḇel – no object is to be left,’</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [18] <dq>And they are going to take away some of your sons who are to be born to you, whom you bring forth, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the sovereign of Baḇel.’</dq> ” [19] And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you have spoken is good!” And he said, “Is it not so, if peace and truth are to be in my days?”

readings.title: The Humbling and the Hedge
readings.subtitle: Ḥizqiyahu and Yerushalayim repent of their self-elevation, establishing a temporary hedge of protection that defers the execution of YeHoVaH's retributive wrath.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 32:26] Then Ḥizqiyahu humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so that the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not come upon them in the days of Ḥizqiyahu.
